subject: Urban Planning
title: Water Recycling: From Toilet to Tap
description: A quick win: understand Water Recycling: From Toilet to Tap.

hook.text: Singapore drinks recycled sewage. They call it NEWater, and it supplies 40% of the nation's water demand.

buildup.text: Treated wastewater passes through microfiltration, reverse osmosis, and UV disinfection. It's purer than most tap water.

discovery.text: Orange County, California has recycled wastewater for decades. The water recharges aquifers and is pumped back as drinking water.

twist.text: The 'yuck factor' is the biggest barrier. Scientifically, recycled water is safe. Psychologically, people reject toilet-to-tap.

climax.text: As droughts worsen, more cities adopt water recycling. Los Angeles plans to recycle 100% of its wastewater by 2035.

punchline.text: All water on Earth is recycled. We're just speeding up the process.

quiz.question: What is the main barrier to water recycling adoption?
options: The technology cannot remove all contaminants effectively
Recycled water costs more than traditional water treatment
